# Tailscale Kubernetes Operator — Service Exposure Behavior

Discovered while deploying a KasmVNC desktop workload on a k3s cluster, 2026-06.

## Exposing a ClusterIP Service on the tailnet

Annotating a ClusterIP Service with `tailscale.com/expose: "true"` causes the
Tailscale operator to provision a dedicated tailnet device for that Service.
The device listens on the Service's `port` value and forwards traffic to
`targetPort` on the backing pods.

The tailnet URL's port equals the Service `spec.ports[].port`. Consequences:

- `port: 8730` → `rsync://hostname.tailnet.ts.net:8730/`
- `port: 443` → `https://hostname.tailnet.ts.net/` (portless, default HTTPS
  port, no `:443` needed in the URL)

Setting `port: 443` is the standard way to get a clean portless HTTPS URL
regardless of which container port the backend actually listens on (e.g. 6901
for KasmVNC).

The device name is set via `tailscale.com/hostname` annotation.

## L4 TCP passthrough — no TLS termination

The operator proxy is L4 TCP passthrough. It does **not** terminate TLS.
A backend serving its own self-signed HTTPS certificate (e.g. KasmVNC on 6901)
reaches the browser as-is, with the self-signed warning intact.

This means:

- `tailscale.com/expose: "true"` + `port: 443` with a self-signed backend →
  browser shows a certificate warning (expected, not a misconfiguration).
- Tailscale HTTPS Certificates (Magic DNS cert provisioning) can eliminate the
  warning, but it publishes device hostnames to public CT logs — a privacy
  trade-off, not a technical limitation.
